sources: Names, descriptions and grades: Exophase (Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophies). PSN progress targets: PSNProfiles (trophies 43531). Guides: written for this page from the official descriptions; where a place or step is not pinned down by a source, the guide says so.

phases.title: Story
phases.blurb: Play Chapters 1 to 4 and the final mission. Story trophies pop as the plot moves; keep a save before the finale.

phases.title: Stranger strands
phases.blurb: Meet the strangers of Leonida and finish each one's chain of jobs, ending in a final mission.

phases.title: Activities
phases.blurb: Sample every activity, then master the ones with counts: range, races, fishing, bowling, meditation, challenges.

phases.title: Collectibles and exploration
phases.blurb: See all 52 areas, pick up the card sets, WAiNK every spot, discover vehicles and register them.

phases.title: Crime and partner
phases.blurb: Robberies, getaways and partner jobs. The timing-sensitive trophies live here — save first, every time.

phases.title: Money and property
phases.blurb: Launder marked bills, spend across the shops and buy all eight garages.

phases.title: 100% cleanup and platinum
phases.blurb: Mop up whatever the checklist still shows, reach 100% completion, and the platinum follows.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.brief: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one unlocks by itself.
trophies.guide: There is no separate task behind the platinum: it arrives the moment the last of the other 54 is earned. Use it as the checklist's finish line rather than a goal of its own. The two golds — the final mission and 100% completion — are the real work; clear the phases in order and this trophy will be waiting at the end.
steps: Work the seven roadmap phases in order, ticking trophies off as they pop.
Leave 100% completion for last; when it pops, the platinum pops with it.
trophies.tip: If only a handful of trophies are left, sort the list by difficulty and clear the easy ones first for momentum.
trophies.risk: Not missable. It unlocks on its own once the other 54 are earned, at any point in the game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)
PSNProfiles — trophies 43531

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.brief: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing opens the game, so this is likely the first trophy on your list. Play the mission the way the game teaches it — movement, driving and the partner system are all introduced here — and see it through to the results screen. A failed attempt costs nothing: replay the mission and finish it cleanly.
steps: Start the story and follow the opening mission's objectives.
Reach the results screen; the trophy pops on completion.
trophies.tip: Treat the opening as a tutorial — there is no reason to rush it.
trophies.risk: Safe if missions can be replayed. Replay has not been confirmed in the game yet, so finish it cleanly the first time.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.brief: Play through every mission in Chapter 1.
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is a run of story missions, and the trophy lands when the chapter closes. Stick to the story missions and save the side content for later — the chapter only ends when its missions do. The official description does not name the closing mission, so the in-game chapter screen is the best place to see what is left.
steps: Follow the story missions in the order the game offers them.
Finish the chapter's last mission; the trophy pops as the chapter ends.
trophies.tip: Check the chapter screen between missions so no side detour delays the ending.
trophies.risk: Nothing in the description makes this missable, as long as chapters can be replayed — replay is still unconfirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.brief: Play through every mission in Chapter 2.
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is a milestone on the road, not a test of skill: reaching its end is the whole requirement. Keep playing the story missions in order and the chapter will close on its own. Neither the mission list nor the chapter's length appears in the official description, and neither is confirmed in the game yet, so no mission names are given here.
steps: Play Chapter 2's story missions in order.
Finish the chapter's closing mission to close the chapter.
trophies.tip: Stock up on supplies before the chapter's bigger jobs; the difficulty climbs from here.
trophies.risk: Safe on a replayable chapter, by the description's wording — though whether chapters replay has not been confirmed in-game yet.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.brief: Play through every mission in Chapter 3.
trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 most of the map and most systems are open, which makes wandering tempting — but the chapter only ends when its missions end. Play the story missions as the game offers them and watch for the chapter-closing beat. The official description names no missions, so none are named here; one clean run through the chapter is enough.
steps: Work through Chapter 3's missions in the order offered.
Finish the closing mission; the trophy follows the chapter end.
trophies.tip: Use the open map between missions to pick up nearby collectibles, but do not let them stall the chapter.
trophies.risk: By its description this is only missable if chapters cannot be replayed; replay is not yet confirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.brief: Play through every mission in Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter.
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last numbered chapter, and the story stacks its harder missions here — go in supplied and save before the big jobs. How many missions the chapter holds, and which one ends it, is not in the official description and is not confirmed in-game yet. Complete the chapter and the trophy pops as the story turns toward its finale.
steps: Save before the chapter's major missions.
Play the chapter through to its end; the trophy pops with the chapter close.
trophies.tip: Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter in case a mission goes badly.
trophies.risk: The description gives no reason to call this missable, if chapter replay exists — and replay is still unconfirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.brief: Finish the final mission to earn a gold.
trophies.guide: The final mission comes after Chapters 1 to 4 and every mission leading into the finale, so it is the story's endpoint. Before starting it, save, stock up, and clear any side content you care about — the description does not say what the game allows after the credits. It does not name the final mission either, so none is named here. Play it through to the end credits and the trophy should appear with the results screen.
steps: Save manually before the finale and clear side content you care about.
Play the final mission through to the credits.
trophies.tip: The choices trophy hints the story may branch — keep a save from before the finale.
trophies.risk: Safe from its description if the final mission can be replayed; replay is unconfirmed in-game. Keep a save before the finale.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.brief: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run.
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, so it arrives in the course of the chapters rather than as something you can trigger early. Keep following the story until the game offers it. The description says nothing about where it starts, what it asks, or which chapter it belongs to, and none of that is confirmed in-game yet — so no walkthrough step is given here. Play it when offered, finish its objectives, and the trophy pops at the results screen.
steps: Keep playing the story until Breakfast Run is offered.
Finish the mission's objectives to the results screen.
trophies.tip: If a mission attempt fails, retry it — a failed attempt still counts once you finish.
trophies.risk: Fine from its description if missions replay; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.brief: Complete the heist mission The Cartel Heist.
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a heist mission, and heists usually ask for preparation — a plan, a crew choice or a vehicle — before the job itself. The official description confirms none of that: no starting point, no prep list, no chapter, and none of it is confirmed in-game yet. Reach the mission through the story, follow its objectives as they appear, and expect a multi-stage job. The trophy pops when the heist mission completes, not when the planning starts.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist through the story.
Do any preparation the mission offers, then play the job through to completion.
trophies.tip: Save before the heist starts; heist missions tend to be long.
trophies.risk: Nothing here suggests it can be missed, if missions can be replayed — replay is still unconfirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.brief: Complete the story mission Child's Play.
trophies.guide: Child's Play is one of the named story missions, so it shows up in the course of the chapters. The description gives no location, no objectives and no chapter for it, and none of those details is confirmed in-game yet, so there is no honest walkthrough to offer here. When the mission appears, play it through to its conclusion and the trophy will pop. If you are unsure whether you have reached it yet, check your mission log for the name.
steps: Follow the story until Child's Play appears in your mission log.
Play it through to its conclusion.
trophies.tip: The mission log is the reliable way to tell whether you have reached a named mission yet.
trophies.risk: Safe as described, assuming missions can be replayed — which has not yet been confirmed in-game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.brief: Complete the story mission Headliners.
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission, and its title suggests a high-profile job — but the official description says nothing about what the mission involves, where it starts, or which chapter it sits in, and none of that is confirmed in-game yet. The safe way to approach it is the same as any named story mission: keep playing the story until it is offered, save before you start, and follow the objectives the game shows you. The trophy pops when the mission's results screen appears, so a failed attempt that you retry still counts.
steps: Play the story until Headliners is offered.
Save first, then finish the mission's objectives.
trophies.tip: A failed attempt is free — retry the mission rather than worrying about a perfect first run.
trophies.risk: By the description, only un-replayable missions could make this missable — and replay is unconfirmed in-game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.brief: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown at the airport.
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a job at the Vice City International Airport. The name points to the airport, but the description does not confirm the mission's starting point, its objectives or its chapter, so this guide does not invent them. Reach it through the story, and when it starts, expect airport security and a getaway to feature — that is a guess from the name alone, not a confirmed step. Finish the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown through the story.
Play the mission through; expect security and a getaway.
trophies.tip: Keep a fast vehicle in mind for the getaway before the mission starts.

trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory sounds like a large set-piece from its military-style name, but the description gives no objectives, no location and no chapter, and none of that is confirmed in-game yet. Do not go looking for it on the map: named missions arrive through the story. When it is offered, save first, stock up, and play through its stages as the game presents them. The trophy pops when the mission completes, so a failed first attempt that you retry is no problem.
steps: Wait for Operation Savage Glory to be offered in the story.
Save, stock up, and play its stages through to completion.
trophies.tip: Set-piece missions are long — clear an evening before you start one.
trophies.risk: Safe on its wording, if missions can be replayed — replay is still unconfirmed in-game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.brief: Reach 100% completion — the game's own checklist, all finished.
trophies.guide: 100% completion is the game's own checklist covering story, side content, activities and collectibles, all finished. This is the long gold trophy and the real gate before the platinum. What exactly counts toward the 100% is not listed in the official description, and that list is not confirmed in-game yet, so this guide cannot spell it out. The practical approach: finish the story, then work down this page's checklist — stranger strands, activities, collectibles, exploration — and watch the in-game completion percentage climb. Leave this trophy for last and let it be the summary of everything else.
steps: Finish the story first, then clear the stranger strands and activities.
Work the collectibles and exploration counts, watching the in-game percentage climb.
trophies.tip: Use the in-game completion percentage as your compass — when it stalls, the checklist here shows what is left.
trophies.risk: Cannot be missed: completion is chased after the story ends, as far as the official description shows.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.brief: Land 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime, drifts.
trophies.guide: A stunt is a driving feat — a jump, a near miss, a long spell of airtime, a drift — and the tally grows as you play. The smart way is to weave stunts into everything else: hit the ramps and hills you pass while travelling, and treat every long drive as practice. The description never defines exactly which moves count, and that definition is not confirmed in-game yet, so watch the counter after different moves to learn what the game rewards. 250 sounds huge, but it builds up over a full playthrough.
steps: Weave stunts into normal travel: ramps, hills and long jumps on the way.
Watch the counter after different moves to learn what the game counts.
trophies.tip: Do not farm stunts in one sitting — let the count grow across the whole playthrough.
trophies.risk: Safe to leave for later: stunts are a count you can keep adding to anywhere, any time.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)
PSNProfiles — trophies 43531 (PSN target of 250)

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.brief: Try every activity type once — nine of them in total.
trophies.guide: This one rewards breadth, not skill: a single attempt at each activity is enough, no win or high score needed. Run through what the game offers — racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest — and tick each off as you find it. The nine types are never named in the official description, and the list is not confirmed in-game yet, so let the in-game activities menu be your checklist. Try one of everything and it pops.
steps: Open the in-game activities menu to see what is on offer.
Try one of each type — a single attempt is enough, no win needed.
trophies.tip: Do this early: it teaches you every system the later trophies use.
trophies.risk: Safe: the activities stay open after the story, as far as the official description shows.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.brief: Take gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: This is the game's pure aim test and one of the toughest silvers: each of the 42 challenges wants a gold medal, not merely a pass. Head to the shooting range, study each challenge's targets and time limit, and retry the ones you miss — nothing in the description limits your attempts. Begin with the weapon types you shoot best, use practice runs to learn the timing, and leave the hardest challenges until your aim is warmed up. Where the range sits and which challenges it holds are not pinned down by the official description, so check the in-game range menu.
steps: Find the shooting range and open its challenge list.
Clear the weapon types you shoot best first, then warm up on the hard ones.
Retry any challenge that misses gold — attempts are unlimited.
trophies.tip: Gold needs speed and accuracy together — learn a challenge's target order before pushing for time.
trophies.risk: Safe: range challenges can be attempted again, as far as the official description shows.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)
PSNProfiles — trophies 43531 (PSN target of 42 challenges)

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.brief: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at each of the 14 locations.
trophies.guide: Drone racing lives or dies on the racing line: learn a course's gates before pushing for speed, and spend the first lap memorising the turns. One win is not enough — every location needs its own victory, so clear them one at a time and tick them off. The description never names the 14 locations or where a race begins, and that is not confirmed in-game yet, so use the in-game activity map to find them. Losing costs nothing but time: run it again until you win.
steps: Find each drone race location on the in-game activity map.
Learn a course's gates on a slow first run, then race for the win.
Clear locations one at a time; each needs its own victory.
trophies.tip: A slow learning lap beats three crashed fast laps — memorise the gates first.
trophies.risk: Safe: a drone race at any location can be run again after a loss.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.brief: Win 20 different races — repeats of the same race do not count.
trophies.guide: Different is the operative word: twenty wins in the same race do not count — you need twenty distinct race events won. Choose the vehicle class and race type you are strongest in, learn the routes, and clear the race list methodically instead of repeating a favourite. Which races count and where they start is not stated in the official description, and that is not confirmed in-game yet, so treat the in-game race menu as your list. A win is a win — you need to finish first, not beat a record.
steps: Open the in-game race menu and pick your strongest vehicle class.
Win races one by one, ticking each distinct event off the list.
Do not repeat a favourite — repeats add nothing to the count.
trophies.tip: Learn one route properly before racing it; a known corner beats a faster car.
trophies.risk: Safe: races can be retried and replayed, per the official description.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophies (name, description, grade)

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.brief: Out-fish Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is a rival angler, and this is a head-to-head contest, not free fishing — you have to find Cal and take him on rather than just catching fish alone. Where Cal fishes, when the challenge opens up, and how it is scored are all unstated in the official description, and none of it is confirmed in-game yet. Practise fishing first until casting and reeling feel natural, then challenge him once you are confident. Lose, and the description gives no reason to think you cannot try again.
steps: Practise fishing until casting and reeling feel natural.
Find Cal and take on his fishing challenge.
trophies.tip: Do not challenge Cal cold — a few practice catches first make the contest far easier.
trophies.risk: Safe: nothing in the description suggests the challenge cannot be retried.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.brief: Finish one arcade game, start to end.
trophies.guide: Find an arcade machine, pick any game on it, and play it through to the end — what matters is completing it, not a high score. The arcade games are not named in the official description, nor are the machines' locations or what counts as completing a game, and none of that is confirmed in-game yet. Pick the shortest or simplest game on the machine, learn its controls from its own instructions, and finish a full run. Once you find a machine, this is one of the easiest trophies on the list.
steps: Find an arcade machine out in the world.
Pick the shortest game on it and play a full run to the end.
trophies.tip: Read the game's own instructions before you start — each arcade game has its own controls.
trophies.risk: Safe: arcade games can be played again.

trophies.brief: Finish the last mission in Andy's stranger strand.

Where Andy is, how many missions his strand holds, and what the final mission asks are all unstated in the official description, and none of it is confirmed in-game yet. Watch for his marker on the map, finish each job he offers, and the trophy pops at the end of the strand.
steps: Find Andy in the world and take his missions as they come.
Work through the strand in order until the final mission appears, then finish it.

Finish the strand's final mission.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.brief: Finish eight full stranger strands across Leonida.
trophies.guide: A strand is a chain of side missions for one character — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have one, and more are out there to find. Finish a strand fully — a half-finished strand does not count — and keep count on this page.
steps: Finish the five named strands: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone.
Explore for three more strangers, watching for their markers.
Complete each strand to its final mission before moving on.
trophies.tip: Five named strands are not enough for eight — keep exploring after the familiar faces are done.

trophies.brief: Hunt down a unique animal for Bret.

Track the unique animal, get into range, and take a clean shot.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.brief: Finish three collectible card sets.
trophies.guide: Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set only counts once you hold every card in it — so this is a scavenger hunt with a checklist. Take one set at a time, search its locations, and keep track of which cards you still need. How many cards are in a set, how many sets exist, and where the cards are — none of that is in the official description, and none of it is confirmed in-game yet. Pair the search with exploring the 52 areas: you will pass card locations on the way. Three full sets is the goal.
steps: Pick one card set and search its locations first.
